hero.subtitle: We defend the agreement that residents deserve genuine voice and consent in the decisions that shape their lives, and we work to hold institutions accountable when they break it.

petition.label: Unofficial Petition
petition.headline: Tell UDOT: the public does not support these cameras.
petition.body: UDOT's permit agreement with the license-plate-reader company says UDOT may terminate it if “UDOT determines that the public does not support the Company’s activities.” That is the opening. Add your name and help us show UDOT that Utah does not support these cameras on our roads.
petition.form_intro: Add your name to the record UDOT will see. First name, last name, ZIP code and email are required; address and phone are optional. Utah residents are what UDOT weighs, but anyone may sign.
petition.consent: By signing this petition you agree to be included in future communications regarding our fight for Utahns.
petition.thanks_title: Thank you for helping us tell UDOT not to enable a surveillance state.
petition.thanks_body: In order to solidify this into law, $25 will help us carry this fight through the legislature.

mission.quote: "Ensuring residents have genuine voice and consent in the decisions that shape their lives and building the civic capacity to make it stick."

about.title: Why Utah Civic Compact?
about.body1: A compact is a mutual obligation between a community and the institutions that govern it. Utah Civic Compact was founded on the belief that this agreement has eroded, and that residents deserve an organization explicitly dedicated to restoring and defending it.
about.body2: We are organized under Section 501(c)(4) as a social welfare organization. That means our mission is the health of Utah communities, not electoral advantages for any party or candidate.
about.body3: We believe in building the long-term infrastructure that makes democracy resilient: informed residents, accountable institutions, and communities with the capacity to hold the line.
about.quote: "Democracy is not a spectator sport. The relationship between Utahns and their government only holds when residents show up organized, informed, and ready to act."

join.title: The Compact Needs You
join.body: Whether you're a longtime civic activist or just getting started, Utah Civic Compact is your home. Sign up to receive updates, action alerts, and opportunities to defend the agreement between Utah communities and their government.
join.item1: Stay informed on the issues that matter
join.item2: Take action when the compact is threatened
join.item3: Connect with others in your community
join.item4: Build lasting civic capacity in Utah

donate.label: Support the Work
donate.title: Fund the Compact
donate.body: Utah Civic Compact runs on community support. Every dollar received means more resources dedicated to public records requests, investigation, and organizing.

modal.title: We need your help.
modal.body: Data centers are consuming Utah's already limited water and power without community consent. Help us fight back before it's too late.
